MW_GAMES_entry.name: Arrhythmix
MW_GAMES_entry.weeklyLine: A new ECG every Thursday. Strip or 12-lead, you’ll know it when you see it.
MW_GAMES_entry.tagline: ECG Thursday: one ECG, six diagnoses, three tries. Read the rhythm.
MW_GAMES_entry.quip: Squiggles in, diagnosis out. Calipers optional.
MW_GAMES_entry.helpQuip: “Sinus rhythm” is not a personality. Read the strip.
help: Read the short case and the ECG, then pick the diagnosis from six options.
You get three tries. Each wrong pick unlocks a hint.
Tap Zoom (or the ECG) to enlarge it. Standard paper: 25 mm/s and 10 mm/mV, so one small square is 40 ms and 0.1 mV.
One new ECG every Thursday. Difficulty varies week to week (rhythm strips are usually gentler, 12-leads harder) and is shown on the badge.
After you finish, Key features highlights what to look for on the trace.
Released at midnight Sydney time each Thursday. Past ECGs live in the archive.

arrhythmix: Arrhythmix is a weekly ECG quiz: ECG Thursday. Every Thursday brings a short fictional case and an ECG drawn on standard ECG paper. Pick the diagnosis from six options in three tries; wrong picks unlock hints, and every answer comes with the key features highlighted on the trace and a teaching pearl.
Students, nurses, paramedics, doctors and anyone learning ECGs. Difficulty varies week to week: rhythm strips are usually gentler, 12-leads harder. The badge on each ECG shows how hard it is.
No. Every trace is computer-generated from parameters to show the textbook features, and every case is fictional. General education, not medical advice.
